sections.title: What the cache is for
sections.body: `LruCache` keeps at most `capacity` items and forgets the one used **longest ago**.

options.text: It builds a cache that stores nothing.
options.why: A zero-capacity cache is refused, not accepted.

options.text: It builds a cache of unlimited size.
options.why: Nothing in the code treats 0 as unlimited.

checkpoints.explanation: The guard in `__init__` raises before any state exists.

checkpoints.prompt: Which methods mark a key as recently used?

options.why: A hit moves the key to the end.
Every write moves the key to the end.
Counting items does not touch their order.

sections.title: How eviction works
sections.body: After each `put`, the cache drops the **first** item of its ordered dict when it is over capacity.

checkpoints.prompt: Which line removes the least recently used item?
checkpoints.explanation: `popitem(last=False)` pops from the front, where the oldest key sits.

final.explanation: Capacity 1 means `a` is evicted when `b` arrives.

options.why: Capacity is not the item count.

final.prompt: Put the steps of `put` in order.
steps: Store the value under the key
Move the key to the end
Evict the oldest item if over capacity

final.prompt: Why does `get` move the key to the end even though it only reads?
final.model_answer: Reading counts as use; moving the key keeps recently read items away from the eviction end.
rubric: Says a read counts as a use
Links the end of the dict to the most recently used position
Links the front of the dict to eviction
